items.reason: FLT_LOG_LEN=16 is the length of flt_log ring buffer used by log_fault(): flt_log[flt_idx++ & (FLT_LOG_LEN - 1)] = code;.
k_trip_a=15.0f A rms is the overload trip level used in prot_slow(): if (i_rms > k_trip_a) then increment ol_ms and after hold time trip/log FLT_OL.
ol_hold_ms=5000 ms is the required time above k_trip_a before shutdown in prot_slow(): if (++ol_ms >= ol_hold_ms) { inv_off(); log_fault(FLT_OL); }.
Inline literal 21.2f is used in prot_fast(): if (a > 21.2f) where a=abs(i_pk) then inv_off() and log_fault(FLT_OC). This is a fast peak-current shutdown threshold.
Inline literal 0.9f is used as vo_rms < 0.9f * VO_NOM to trigger FLT_BRN (brown/undervoltage warning/fault). It is a fraction of VO_NOM, not an absolute regulation band edge.
Inline literal 3 is the max retry count in prot_restart(): if (retry < 3) { delay_ms(500); retry++; inv_on(); }.
Inline literal 500 is the delay passed to delay_ms(500) before inv_on() during restart attempts in prot_restart(). It is a restart wait time, not an overload delay.
FW_VER_MAJ (line 19) is firmware major version identifier; used as an ID, not a physical spec.
VIN_LO_XFER (line 22) is the AC input window lower transfer point (go to battery below this, Vrms).
VIN_HI_XFER (line 23) is the AC input window upper transfer point (go to battery above this, Vrms).
VBUS_REF (line 26) is PFC regulation target (V). It is the bus regulation setpoint; closest spec rule is vbus_set (though the rule mentions rounding/margins, while this file uses 400.0f directly).
VO_NOM (line 29) is nominal output voltage, Vrms, i.e., the output regulation setpoint candidate; spec rule vout_set is the output RMS setpoint.
VO_TOL (line 30) is the allowable regulation band tolerance as +/- fraction; it is not itself a setpoint band edge rule id (the derived edges are).
VO_HI (line 31) computes the upper regulation band edge as VO_NOM * (1.0 + VO_TOL). This directly maps to vout_hi.
IO_RATED (line 32) is rated output current (A rms, 1500 VA / 120 V).
I_TRIP_RMS (line 33) is overload shutdown current level (A rms). This matches the software trip threshold rule iout_trip (timed; delay not present in this file).
TMR_LD (line 36) is PWM period register described as 'PWM period, 25 kHz carrier'; the constant is the period-count value (TBPRD-like). Spec rule is pwm_period (counts).
DB_CNT (line 37) is dead-time register ('300 us dead time'), and the constant itself is the deadband count value; maps to pwm_deadband (counts).
K_P (line 40) is voltage loop proportional gain; maps to vloop_kp.
K_I (line 41) is voltage loop integral gain per control ISR; maps to vloop_ki.
VBAT_NOM (line 44) is battery string nominal voltage, V; maps to vbat_nom.
VBAT_CUT (line 45) is end-of-discharge / low-battery shutdown voltage; maps to vbat_cutoff.
UART_BAUD (line 48) is UART baud rate for front-panel / RS-232 port; category is comms_or_buffer.
PIN_BYP_RELAY (line 49) is a GPIO number for static bypass relay drive; category is pin_map.

ADC_FULL is the ADC full-scale code (4095.0f). It is used in the bus scaling chain via K_VS = VBUS_FS / ADC_FULL, so it defines the ADC full-scale count for the vbus sense path (vbus_fs is the bus voltage corresponding to ADC full scale).

DAC_FULL is the comparator reference DAC full-scale code (4095). It is used to form the negative comparator threshold code CMP_DAC_LO = (DAC_FULL - CMP_DAC_HI), so it is a comparator-DAC range constant, not directly a regulated physical quantity.
VBUS_FS (498.3f) is the DC bus voltage at ADC full scale (“V at ADC full scale”). This directly matches vbus_fs.
K_VS = (VBUS_FS / ADC_FULL) is the voltage per ADC count derived from the bus divider full-scale. This matches vbus_scale (volts of bus per ADC count).
VBAT_FS (168.0f) is the battery voltage at ADC full scale (“V at ADC full scale”). This matches vbat_fs.
VO_FS_PK (501.6f) is the peak output voltage at the edge of the mid-rail-biased sense range (“output voltage, mid-rail biased… peak V at +/- half scale”). This matches vout_fs_pk.
IO_FS_PK (33.0f) is the peak output current at the edge of the mid-rail-biased current-sense range (“peak A at +/- half scale”). This matches iout_fs_pk.
CMP_DAC_HI (3364) is the comparator DAC code for the positive overcurrent/peak-current trip (“positive overcurrent trip code”). This corresponds to iout_pklim_dac_hi.
CMP_DAC_LO = (DAC_FULL - CMP_DAC_HI) is the negative comparator DAC code for the hardware peak-current limit, forming the opposite side threshold. This corresponds to iout_pklim_dac_lo.
